symptom: rdb-divergence-workflow.md says the operation arguments were in rsi and rdx, based on the issue #8 demo. For ChaCha20Poly1305::encryption_output_length(&self, usize) -> Result<usize, CryptoError>, the 16-byte Result is returned through a hidden pointer in rdi, so rsi holds &self and rdx holds the length. 'variable list' prints only stack-slot addresses. In the original session they changed between runs (0x7ffc42b2d5d0 vs 0x7ffe44964460), but the #49 replay saw identical addresses across runs, so whether rdb disables ASLR depends on the environment; read memory only at an address printed earlier in the same session. The break address itself is build-specific (0x2111f0 originally; 0x211240, 0x211250, 0x2111e0 in clean rebuilds).
repro_cmd: nix develop path:/home/goya/storage/full-ligature-port-workspace#crypto-mixed -c oracle/divergences/boundary-aead-output-length-encrypt-0003/replay.sh   # the transcript shows rdi (hidden return pointer), rsi (&self) and rdx (the length)
expected: The length argument in rsi, as in the workflow demo.
actual: rsi holds &self and rdx = 0x3fffffffc1 (the length); rdi is the hidden return pointer. Stack-slot addresses moved between runs in the original session but not in the #49 replay.
workaround: Read the argument registers from the target's ABI: a Rust function returning an aggregate wider than two registers takes a hidden return pointer in rdi. 'expression' is still unsupported.
revisit_trigger: When rdb gains expression evaluation or value printing for 'variable'
